_meta.note: Two distinct deeplink namespaces exist, and this manifest's `inputs` describe namespace (2) unless a `hash_params` field says otherwise: (1) `tools/<slug>.html#<key>=<val>&...` — the tool's own saveHash()/loadHash() keys, frequently log10 (flagged per-key with "LOG10" in `desc` or "log10": true) and always the raw slider state; (2) `tools/<slug>.html#in=<base64url(JSON)>` — decoded by data/prefill.js into window.OCS_APPLY_PREFILL(obj), which 22 of 35 catalog tools define, and which always takes LINEAR, human-named keys (e.g. mass_solar, distance_kpc) regardless of what the underlying hash key or its units are. `inputs` in this manifest documents namespace (2)'s keys when a tool defines OCS_APPLY_PREFILL; where namespace (1)'s hash keys differ in name and/or scale from the `inputs` keys, a `hash_params` field lists the real hash keys with their log10 flags. Tools with no `hash_params` field and no divergence note use the same keys/scale in both namespaces.
_meta.chainsNote: The chains below are narrative reading paths, not machine-executable workflows: every entry is the identical shape {page, register, steps, tier, title}, and every step carries only {tool, handoff} — handoff is English prose describing what a human reader should do with the prior tool's output, never a structured output-to-input mapping. They exist to guide a reader (or an agent reading prose) through a sequence of pages, not to be executed as a pipeline. The MCP worker's actual machine-executable chains are a small, separate, disjoint set — imbh-evidence-window, evidence-threshold-routing, accretion-eligibility-fastfail — reachable via the run_chain tool, with real structured step inputs (fields) and decision gates (gate.rules). None of those three worker chain ids appear among the catalog chains below, and none of the catalog chains below are runnable via run_chain.

scenario-paper-e-feasibility.title: Paper E, Walked: Envelope to Adjudication

steps.handoff: Monte Carlo sweep shows flybys never bind the envelope; median diffusion floor ~3e9 yr across the swept radius range.
Single-point drill-down at a radius chosen from the swept envelope returns the full encounter-rate and orbit budget.
Bondi supply vs. waste-heat ceiling ordering shows thermal concealment binds, not fuel, at the fiducial transport floor.
Waste-heat channel routed as 2*ln BF adjudicates today's data: ln K = -0.40, supports null hypothesis.

scenario-migrate-or-stay.title: Migrate or Stay: The Discount-Rate Verdict

steps.handoff: Closed-form migrate-vs-densify crossover: rho* = 2.00e-4 yr^-1 at the fiducial destination gain, transit survival, and transit time.
Weitzman gamma-discounting under a two-point prior over the discount rate: rho_eff either clears or stays above the Step 1 threshold depending on the prior's horizon and weighting.
Concrete wait-vs-act verdict given a real engine: a large IMBH platform favors acting now, a small one favors aestivation, independent of the discount-rate verdict alone.
Poisson background accounting behind Paper A's T6 kill condition: a quiet field is background-free by many orders of magnitude, a busy field is marginal once a trials-factor penalty is applied.

LISA/Fermi-LAT/CTA/KM3NeT coincidence score for the same IMBH mass range: 4/4 channels detected regardless of environment at OC's distance, since any transient in the tool's allowed power range clears every threshold.
Follow-up campaign sized off the Step 1 background result: ELT-MICADO confirmation for the quiet field, Roman discovery-goal search for the busy field.
